added_failure_basis: The reviewed run r-20261020T204942364841-shc-locus-remeasure recorded no suite: its manifest baseline_suite and after_suite keys are empty and its tests: line reads "none", so there are no gate logs to derive failure ids from and the added-failure measure had no baseline to compare against. The count of 0 is therefore an absent measurement rather than a measured zero; no failing test id exists on either side to name.

findings.text: blocking: the record carries no run call count, so the node's own done-when figure "calls" is unrecorded. Line 16 is the spend_usd line of the single applies entry, where the sibling figure belongs; estimate_basis.calls 36 is the estimate basis over 22 prior runs and planned_calls 5 is the dry run's plan, neither of which is the run's calls. The predecessor record for the same section (shc-three-family-measure-results.json) carries llm_cost_rows with a per-phase calls count even for its interrupted attempt, so the format exists, and the figure exists here -- the manifest's checkpoint names 9 LLMCost rows in run e0509ebe -- so the omission is a repairable gap in the node's own quantitative measure rather than an unobtainable number. The html at shc-locus-remeasure.html:4 omits it as well.

follow-on: record_apply's docstring states "The spend is the campaign summary's total_cost, which apportions the run's LLMCost rows", but the function takes spend from the --spend argument at line 229 and never reads total_cost from the summary it parses at lines 194-206, so the docstring describes provenance the code does not implement.

follow-on: the run paragraph asserts the spend was read "from the run's LLMCost documentation-phase rows read while the graph was reachable", but no committed artefact carries that query or its output -- apply-1.log has no cost line -- so the USD 0.4055 is stated on the strength of uncommitted run-directory scratch scripts (spend.py, attr.py) that a reader cannot open from the record.
